newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds retain a positive glow pre-data.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds retain a positive glow pre-data.

text.p: *Australian bond yields remained close to last week's 3-1/2 year lows in readiness for what is expected to be extremely friendly data this week for inflation and wages.
*Turnover relatively light, partly due to Japanese holiday.
Australian 10-year bond yields remained close to last week's 3-1/2 year lows in readiness for what is expected to be extremely market friendly data this week for inflation and wages.

However, turnover was relatively light given the bullish expectations for the data, which could trigger a further easing in monetary policy, although traders said this was partly due to today's Japanese holiday.
Wednesday's second quarter inflation report is expected to show a 0.1 percent fall in the headline CPI for an annual rate of just 0.5 percent, according to a Reuters survey.
The policy-sensitive underlying inflation rate will further bolster the market, seen rising 0.4 percent for a 1.7 percent annual rate and below the Reserve Bank's 2.0-3.0 percent target.

Thursday's second quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) data is also not expected to give the central bank any concern, rising 0.8 percent for an annual rate of 4.1 percent and below the RBA's 4.5 percent 'line in the sand'.
However, one event that could threaten the market's positive mood before the data could be Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony which starts on Tuesday.

Yield spreads to the U.S. narrowed sharply after the U.S. market showed signs of jitters on Friday ahead of Greenspan's testimony. The 10-year yield spread is seen compressing further on confirmation of Australia's current superior inflation record over the U.S.
